findings.obligation: E1: when a scan cannot write its results to the store, the run ends Interrupted and never reports itself as Completed - the promised outcome must be observed failing for its own reason, not only the absence of its test seam.
findings.observation: The recorded RED is the development build refusing the fault name at startup (review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:85), so then_the_scan_ended_interrupted, the queue's absent-count assertions and then_her_queue_counts_exactly have never executed. Nothing on record shows they can fail; the designer's scratch-case report is uncommitted and uncorroborated.
findings.remediation: Within this slice, after config.rs accepts the two fault names and the store refuses the write, but BEFORE scan.rs stops discarding the mark_repo_read / record_account_checks errors, run 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure' once and keep the output showing the failure has moved to then_the_scan_ended_interrupted (status "completed"); only then make it GREEN. If the intermediate state is not reachable, say so with the reason instead of skipping the observation.

observations.text: Re-review scope and commit comparison, d957229 (my accepted record) to the reviewed clean HEAD 94514b3 ('git status --porcelain' empty). 'git log --oneline d957229..HEAD' is the single commit 94514b3 'test(review-app): pin the store-failure oracle's count and resume'. 'git diff --name-only d957229 HEAD' is tests/acceptance/review_app_scan_store_failure.rs plus the nwdes-rendered acceptance.md / acceptance.html / handoff.json. 'git diff --stat d957229 HEAD -- tests/acceptance/support/ crates/ xtask/ Cargo.lock rust-toolchain.toml' is EMPTY: both declared supports, every production crate and the toolchain/lock pins are byte-identical to the revision I last ran, so nothing outside the oracle needed re-checking. The oracle's own bytes changed, so equivalence was not established for the declared command and it was RERUN. I re-reviewed only the three corrected oracle findings and the obligations they touch (E2, E3 and the reuse closure); the E1 closure, the RED classification, the port/boundary judgment and the supports judgment from the accepted d957229 record are retained unchanged, and nothing in this delta bears on them. The rendered acceptance delta was checked for drift: the S1 criterion rows now read 'offers only to resume it', 'picks that same run up rather than starting over' and 'accounts for exactly as many repos as the resumed scan read, no more and no fewer', and the first row's frozen-plan carve-out sentence is gone - all consistent with the strengthened oracle. Expectations E1-E5 are byte-identical, so the examiner's fixed expectations were not touched.

Run (my own execution, clean HEAD 94514b3): argv 'cargo test -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure', cwd /Users/jeffbailey/Projects/foss/leading/openlore, exit 101. stdout: 'running 4 tests'; 2 passed (the state_delta support self-tests); 2 failed - a_scan_that_cannot_save_that_it_read_a_repo_is_offered_for_resuming and a_scan_that_cannot_save_her_account_checks_is_offered_for_resuming; 'test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 2 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out; finished in 4.59s'; stderr only cargo's own 'error: test failed, to rerun pass -p openlore-review-app --test review_app_scan_store_failure'. No compiler warning or error: the revised oracle compiles, so browser.press and then_scan_reaches_on_its_own resolve and the removed local step left no unused import. Both panics are now at review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:89:49 (the GIVEN, moved four lines by the revision), each carrying the app's own log {"event":"health.startup.refused","probe":"config","reason":"REVIEW_APP_TEST_FAULT is invalid: not a known test fault"}, exit Some(2), for refuse_mark_repo_read and refuse_record_account_checks. The RED is unchanged in kind and reason from the accepted record: semantic, the declared config.rs fault seam absent, not BROKEN. Output kept at /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jeffbailey-Projects-foss-leading-openlore/2e5be832-19d9-47f2-b3d4-a99c5d91a0cd/scratchpad/s1-red-reviewer-94514b3.txt.

Finding 1 (E3, the boundary-less count) is RESOLVED, by reading the revised bytes. then_her_queue_counts_exactly (review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:239-266) no longer calls contains: counts_claimed walks every occurrence of both wordings, takes the whole digit run immediately in front of each (trim_end then reversed take_while on ascii digits, re-reversed and parsed), keeps them in document order and the step asserts assert_eq!(claimed, vec![repos.len()]). The counterexample I recorded now fails as it must: for 5 repos read, a rendered '15 repos read' parses the digit run '15', so claimed [15] != expected [5]. Both directions E3 names are now caught - an over-count and an under-count - and so is a second count line or a missing one, since the comparison is over the whole vector. The singular wording is handled: '1 repo read' parses to [1] against repos.len() 1. The two wordings cannot double-count the same text ('repos read' does not contain 'repo read'). The new failure message keeps WHAT (the claimed vector against the expected one and the repos actually read), WHY (a larger number tells her repos were read that never were, a smaller one hides work she is owed) and HOW (mark each planned repo read as it is read and account for exactly those). The parser reads only rendered page text; it reimplements no production rule, so the oracle stays independent.

Finding 2 (E2, the unbound resume press) is RESOLVED. when_she_resumes (review_app_scan_store_failure.rs:125-151) now captures the interrupted queue once, asserts offers(RESUME_SCAN), asserts over FRESH_SCAN_LABELS = ['Scan again', 'Scan my repos'] that neither is offered beside it, then presses RESUME_SCAN itself and polls with then_scan_reaches_on_its_own(browser, "completed", 60), which presses nothing. The shared when_scan_finishes helper, whose first-matching-label press was the hole, is no longer on the resume path, so the completed run the count is read from is provably the run she resumed and E2's 'resumes that run, instead of starting over' is observed, not assumed. Residual, recorded rather than left implicit: the poll now waits for 'completed' specifically, so a resumed run that ends interrupted again costs the full 60 s before then_the_scan_ended_completed reports it - an honest failure, slower, and the only path on which it is paid. And the new negative assertion requires the interrupted queue to offer no fresh-scan action at all; the designer declared that in the S1 criterion row ('her queue offers only to resume it') and it was the remediation I named, but it is a stronger claim on the queue view than E2's words alone compel. If production has a deliberate reason to offer a fresh scan beside Resume scan, that is a product question for the promise owner, not a test repair.

Finding 3 (the duplicated step) is RESOLVED. The local when_she_scans is deleted; the suite now imports when_scans from review_app::repos_and_accounts and both scenarios call it in the same position, so the step has one home again. SCAN_AGAIN is now FRESH_SCAN_LABELS[0] rather than a second copy of the literal, so the finished-run label is also declared once. Scenario bodies still read as visible composed steps - given_store_refusing, given_owner_ready_to_scan, when_scans, then_the_scan_ended_interrupted, then_her_queue_offers_to_resume_and_claims_no_count, when_the_store_accepts_writes_again, when_she_resumes, then_the_scan_ended_completed, then_the_resume_read_what_was_never_saved, then_her_queue_counts_exactly - with one business stimulus per When and no logic or branching in the bodies.

Retained from the accepted d957229 record, unaffected by this delta and re-confirmed against the revised bytes: the oracle drives only the public surface (the real app process over HTTP, /scan/status, the queue page), with the real store, sign-in, ownership proof and scan, and only GitHub and ATProto doubled; E1 is falsified by then_the_scan_ended_interrupted's strict 'interrupted' plus the absent 'Scan again' on the cut-short queue; the no-count assertions over both wordings still guard the interrupted run; the count is still compared against repos_read_since, an independent oracle built from the GitHub double's request log rather than the store rows production counts from; every assertion still serves a declared promise and both declared refused writes still have one scenario each. Declared supports are untouched since 3fa912a and were not re-examined. Capability limits unchanged: typesafe unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent, exit 3), and the project's test-impact tool returned no selection on either earlier attempt, so this re-review's selection is the change set d957229..94514b3, whose only test file is the oracle itself. Still true, and still the one open obligation: both scenarios die in the GIVEN, so no business assertion of P1 - including the two assertions revised here - has ever executed; the finding owned by implementation carries that observation forward.

diagnostic: APPROVED for craft, re-reviewed on clean HEAD 94514b3, limited to the three corrected oracle findings and the obligations they touch. All three are resolved against the revised bytes and a rerun of the declared command: E3's count is now parsed as whole digit runs and asserted equal, as a whole vector, to exactly the repos the resume read, so the over-count counterexample I recorded ('15 repos read' passing for 5) now fails; E2's resume step asserts no fresh-scan label is offered beside 'Resume scan', presses 'Resume scan' itself and then only polls, so the completed run the count is read from is provably the resumed one; and the duplicated local step is gone in favour of repos_and_accounts::when_scans. The rerun at 94514b3 is exit 101, 2 passed / 2 failed in 4.59 s, both scenarios failing in the GIVEN at line 89 on the same semantic RED as before - the app's config probe refusing refuse_mark_repo_read / refuse_record_account_checks, declared S1 behaviour of crates/openlore-review-app/src/config.rs - with no compiler warning or error. Supports and production are byte-identical since 3fa912a and were not re-examined; expectations E1-E5 are byte-identical, so the examiner's fixed expectations were not touched, and the rendered S1 criterion rows now match the strengthened oracle. Judgments retained from the accepted d957229 record: public-port boundary, E1 closure, the independent count oracle, both declared refused writes covered, and the capability limits (typesafe unavailable; the project's test-impact tool returned no selection). One finding remains open and does not block craft, the one owned by implementation: no business assertion of P1 has yet executed, so the business RED must be observed on then_the_scan_ended_interrupted once the fault seam lands and before scan.rs stops discarding the write errors. Two residuals are recorded rather than raised as findings: the resume poll now waits specifically for 'completed', so a run that ends interrupted again costs the full 60 s before it reports; and the new 'no fresh-scan label' assertion is a stronger claim on the queue view than E2's words alone compel - if production has a deliberate reason to offer a fresh scan beside Resume scan, that is a product question for the promise owner, not a test repair. Implementation GREEN on both scenarios remains a completion obligation.
